Notice of Proposed Action
Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC) Regulations
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Housing Development and Finance Committee
(HDFC) proposes to adopt regulations pursuant to AB 179 (Chapter 69, Statu tes of 2026 )
and the provisions of Part 18 of the Health and Safety Code (HSC) (commencing with
§54920), which establish the HDFC and its Executive Committee and authorize the
consolidated statewide administration of multifamily affordable housing programs.
Pursuant to HSC § 54946(a)(2), this Notice of Proposed Action is issued at least 21 days
prior to the close of the public comment period.
WRITTEN COMMENT PERIOD
Any interested person, or their authorized representative, may submit written comments
relevant to the proposed action to HDFC. The comment period begins October 26, 2026, and
closes at 5:00 p.m. on November 17, 2026. HDFC will consider all comments received during
this timeframe. Please submit comments to HDFCRegComments@hdfc.ca.gov and include
HDFC Regulations Public Comments in the subject line. Written comments can also be sent
via mail to:
Housing Development and Finance Committee
ATTENTION: HDFC Regulations Public Comments
651 Bannon Street, Suite 400
Sacramento, CA 95811
PUBLIC HEARING
A public hearing on the proposed regulations is scheduled on the following:
Date: November 9, 2026
Time: 10:00am – noon
Location: California Bank and Trust 520 Capitol Mall
Lower–Level Conference Room Sacramento, CA 95814
Available via Zoom. HDFC Second Draft Regulations Public Hearing
At the hearing, any person may present statements or arguments orally or in writing relevant to
this proposed action. HDFC requests, but does not require, that persons who provide oral
comments at the hearing also submit a written copy of their testimony at the hearing. HDFC
further requests, but does not require, that you reference the section of the proposed
regulations on which you are commenting in both your oral and written comments.
AUTHORITY AND REFERENCE
This action is taken pursuant to HSC § 54946(a), which authorizes the executive
committee to adopt regulations without complying with the procedural requirements of
Chapter 3.5 (commencing with §11340) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government
Code except for certain notice, comment period duration, public hearing, and final
statement of reasons requirements specified in HSC § 54946(a)(2).
Pursuant to HSC § 54946(c), these regulations will become effective immediately upon
adoption by the executive committee.
INFORMATIVE DIGEST/POLICY STATEMENT OVERVIEW
Assembly Bill 179 (Chapter 68, Statutes of 2026) restructured state oversight of housing-
related bond allocations and established the Housing Development and Finance
Committee . AB 179 provides the statutory framework under which HDFC administers
program requirements, reviews project applications, and facilitates the allocation of certain
private activity bonds and related resources for multifamily affordable housing statewide.
The proposed regulations implement HDFC’s statutory responsibilities by establishing
clear program definitions, administrative procedures, evaluation standards, and
compliance requirements necessary to administer the transferred multifamily housing
programs and operationalize cert ain bond and tax credit reservation process described in
The proposed regulations are intended to enhance statewide consistency in certain
multifamily program administration and improve transparency in allocation and award
processes. These regulations support coordinated procedures across reviewing entities
and provide the structural clari ty needed to carry out HDFC’s statutory mandate under AB
IMPACT OF PROPOSED REGULATIONS
The proposed regulations are expected to strengthen and streamline the administration of
programs overseen by the HDFC. By clarifying program requirements, defining terms and
procedures, and aligning regulatory language with the statutory framework established
under AB 179, these regulations will streamline internal review processes, reduce
administrative redundancies, and improve coordination across participating entities.
The changes are anticipated to enhance predictability for applicants, promote greater
transparency in the interpretation and application of program rules , and promote
consistent statewide implementation of HDFC- administered programs.
EVALUATION OF WHETHER THESE REGULATIONS ARE INCONSISTENT OR
INCOMPATABLE WITH EXISTING STATE REGULATIONS
HDFC’s review has not identified any conflicts or duplications with existing state
regulations.
COMPATIBILITY WITH FEDERAL LAW
HDFC’s review has not identified any comparable federal regulations that directly govern
its statutory responsibilities and therefore has not identified any inconsistencies .
LOCAL MANDATE
HDFC’s review has not identified any basis to conclude that the proposed regulations
impose a mandate on local agencies or school districts requiring state reimbursement
under Gov. Code § 17500 et seq.
FISCAL IMPACT
Cost or savings to any state agency: None anticipated.
Cost to local agencies or school districts: None anticipated.
Other nondiscretionary costs or savings imposed on local agencies: None anticipated.
Cost or savings in federal funding to the state: None anticipated.
EFFECT ON SMALL BUSINESS
Based on the Committee’s review, it has not identified any meaningful impact on small
businesses. The proposed regulations do not impose mandatory obligations or compliance
requirements on small businesses. Participation in the program is voluntary, and
businesses engage only if they choose to apply for and receive funding.
EFFECT ON HOUSING COSTS
Implementation of these regulations and the consolidation of multifamily affordable housing
loan and grant programs combined with other resources administered by the State Treasurer’s
Office, is projected to reduce total housing development costs in the state.
INITIAL DETERMINATION OF STATEWIDE ADVERSE ECONOMIC IMPACT DIRECTLY
AFFECTING BUSINESSES
The proposed regulations do not impose mandatory obligations or compliance
requirements on businesses. Participation in the program is voluntary, and businesses
engage only if they choose to apply for and receive funding. Based on HDFC’s initial
review, it has not identified any significant statewide adverse economic impact directly
affecting businesses, including California businesses’ ability to compete with those in other
states.
COST IMPACTS ON PRIVATE PERSONS OR BUSINESSES DIRECTLY AFFECTED
The proposed regulations do not impose mandatory obligations or compliance
requirements on private persons or businesses. Participation in the program is voluntary,
and private persons or businesses engage only if they choose to apply for and receive
funding. HDFC is not aware of any cost impacts that a representative private person or
business would necessarily incur in reasonable compliance with the proposed action.
CONSIDERATION OF ALTERNATIVES
HDFC has considered alternatives to the proposed regulations and has determined no
other reasonable alternatives would be more effective or less burdensome while achieving
the regulatory objectives. HDFC invites interested persons to submit alternatives for
consideration during the comment period.
AVAILABILITY OF TEXT OF PROPOSED GUIDELINES AND INITIAL STATEMENT OF
REASONS
The proposed regulatory text is available on the HDFC website at: HDFC Regulations –
Housing Development and Finance Committee. Copies may also be requested from the
contact person listed below.
AVAILABILITY OF CHANGED OR MODIFIED TEXT
If changes or modifications are made to the proposed regulations, the modified text will be
made available prior to adoption.
AVAILABILITY OF RULEMAKING DOCUMENTS
A rulemaking file will be maintained, consistent with Gov. Code § 11347.3, including the
proposed regulatory text, final statement of reasons, public comments (if any), and any
modifications. The rulemaking file will be available upon request to the contact person listed
below.
AVAILABILITY OF FINAL STATEMENT OF REASONS
Following adoption, the Final Statement of Reasons (FS OR) will be prepared and made
available to the public upon request to the contact person listed below as required under
Gov. Code § 11346.9(a).
